title: TrustedVolumes RFQ settlement — vulnerable drain selectors rolled back; $0 live extractable

key_facts: Historical loss: $5.87M in tx 0xc5c61b3ac39d854773b9dc34bd0cdbc8b5bbf75f18551802a0b5881fcb990513 (block 25,039,670, 2026-05-07): 1291.16110521587917927 WETH + 206,282.446876 USDT + 16.93910519 WBTC + 1,268,771.488879 USDC pulled from InventoryVault 0x9bA0CF1588E1DFA905eC948F7FE5104dD40EDa31

Registry fully reconstructed from 55 events and matched live getFunctionImplementation() for all 37 selectors (0 mismatches)
Attacker's signer authorization persists on-chain today: isAllowedOrderSigner(helper 0xd4d5..., attacker 0xc3eb...)=true (harmless while selectors unregistered; instantly dangerous if re-extended)

caveats: Unverified bytecode: auth/source conclusions for the RFQ impl rest on exploit trace + decompilation (medium confidence on exact arg order, high on the check/source split)
The 'no registered selector can spend third-party approvals' result is based on decompiled unverified code (corroborated by fork tests and upstream 0x sources), not a formal proof
Cross-chain clones at different addresses cannot be fully excluded; direct checks found none
Dust valuation ($1.1531) uses DefiLlama prices at work time
one_liner: External unprivileged attacker can extract ~$0 live: the vulnerable RFQ selectors (0x4112e1c2 drain and 0xea7faa61 signer registration) were unregistered by the owner on 2026-06-22, all admin functions are owner-gated, and every remaining registered selector is read-only, owner-gated or caller-sourced; the $5.87M exploit is fork-reproducible only on pre-rollback state.
